metadata.title: MAPP 5014.1 Rev.1 Understanding CDER's Risk-Based Site Selection Model
metadata.legal_basis: CDER Manual of Policies and Procedures (internal FDA review procedure). Informative; not binding on applicants.
metadata.applicability: FDA staff procedure. Category: Regulatory Review and Scientific Policies.

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.
limitations: English rule-based extraction; no GPT or paid API.

candidates.statement:  The list of sites prioritized by the model includes sites in the CDER Catalog of Manufacturing Sites that are subject to routine surveillance inspections, as determined by section 510 of the FD&C Act. The CDER Catalog of Manufacturing Sites comprises sites that commercially manufacture a finished pharmaceutical (drug product), an in-process material, or an active pharmaceutical ingredient (API; drug substance) for use in a drug intended for humans.
candidates.context:  The SSM considers risk related to drug quality (for both drug substance and finished product) that may arise from violations of the CGMP requirements in section 501(a)(2)(B) of the FD&C Act (21 U.S.C 351(a)(2)(B)) and related regulations (e.g., 21 CFR parts 210 and 211). 1 In this MAPP, the terms establishment, site, and facility are used interchangeably and cover physical locations subject to FDA drug manufacturing regulations and statutory authority.

candidates.statement: f) The compliance history of establishments in the country or region in which the establishment is located that are subject to regulation under this FD&C Act, including the history of violations related to products exported from such country or region that are subject to such regulation.
candidates.context: e) Whether the establishment has been inspected by a foreign government or an agency of a foreign government recognized under section 809 of the FD&C Act (21 U.S.C. 384e). g) Any other criteria deemed necessary and appropriate by the Secretary for purposes of allocating inspection resources. 4

candidates.statement: 3.3 If the removal is requested because of a change in a site’s operational status (e.g., the site has gone out of business) or discrepancies between FDA’s understanding of the site and the site’s claims (e.g., the site claims to no longer produce drugs for the U.S. market), then the removal can only take place if the OQS investigation confirms that FDA’s information needs to be revised and the discrepancy between FDA and the site is corrected.
